authority: NONE — DERIVED TRUTH. Every value here is a measurement, never a choice.

corrections.reason: Import statements per tracked artifact: 7.964238 -> 7.993862, a rise of 0.029624 across 2281 tracked artifacts. RE-SEEDED for the coverage programme that took the repository from 97.1942% to over 98% under the CD-02 floor, and the rise is that programme's cost stated as a number. Sixteen new test modules were admitted and forty-odd existing suites extended; a test module imports the surface it measures, so it imports more than the average artifact, and admitting one necessarily raises an average taken over all of them. THE METRIC IS WORKING, NOT WRONG: nothing here claims the repository became less tangled. What it records is that the tangle was bought, by whom, and for what. COMPENSATION WAS PERFORMED FIRST AND IS RECORDED. Fifty-three DUPLICATED function-local import statements were hoisted to module level across twenty-one suites - the same import repeated inside twelve test bodies is twelve statements for one edge, so removing the copies removes statements without removing a single edge, and the import graph is byte-identical either way. Two further sites were converted from importlib.import_module with a computed argument to a static import plus a sys.modules lookup, which also returned unresolved_dynamic_sites to its bound of 22. WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: the residual would close by rewriting `from package.module import Name` as `from package import module` across the new suites and rewriting every reference, or by aliasing imported names to module-level assignments. The first trades readability for a counter and the second is a pure evasion of one - both are the gaming the Omega-4 note already refuses, and refusing them is why this entry exists instead. A JUSTIFICATION WOULD HAVE BEEN THE WRONG INSTRUMENT: it permits every future regression on this metric forever, and what happened here was one bounded, law-driven admission. The bound now binds at the new value, so the next module that raises it is refused exactly as this one was.

Surface statements per callable: 6.397527 -> 6.398330, a rise of 0.0008. RE-SEEDED at verification closure. The rise is four import statements and their statements, every one of them required by a LAW rather than chosen: (1) engine/universal_discovery/gate.py gained a main() delegation because UEC-000001 locates every engine/*/gate.py as an enforcement artifact and UEC-L-04 requires it to be invoked by its own module path -- 'nothing enforces by existing'; the alternative was raising the engines_with_no_invoker ceiling from 6 to 7, which is the move Omega-4 exists to refuse. (2) engine/tests/unit/test_certification_integrity.py imports the ratchet module because UCI's six laws are now held to directions rather than ceilings and the tests must supply the sealed state they compare against. (3) engine/tests/unit/test_verification_intelligence.py imports clear_derived_scope_cache and the registry module because the collection set is derived and its fixtures must be real git trees. COMPENSATION WAS ATTEMPTED FIRST AND IS RECORDED: three same-module import statements in surface.py were merged into one node and three function-local imports in the UVI test were hoisted to a single module-level import, recovering five nodes of the nine. Shaving further would be gaming the measurement rather than governing the repository, which is why the remainder is declared here instead of hidden. A JUSTIFICATION WOULD HAVE BEEN THE WRONG INSTRUMENT: it permits every future regression on the metric forever, and what happened here was one bounded, law-driven addition. FINAL VALUE IS THE FORMATTER'S, AND THE TENSION IS RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED IN SECRET: the compensation described above merged three `from engine.universal_discovery import` statements in surface.py into one node, and ruff's import sorting (rule I001, part of the canonical lint gate) requires aliased imports to be split back into separate statements. The lint gate is authoritative for style, so the merge was reverted and the bound is sealed at the count ruff produces. The residual is two import nodes. A repository cannot hold both a formatter that splits imports and a ratchet that counts them without one of them yielding, and the ratchet is the one that yields -- silently fighting the formatter would make every future `ruff format` a governance event.

RE-SEEDED after a MEASUREMENT DEFECT was fixed, not after a regression. The bound was 33 and it was wrong. graph.SCRIPT_INVOCATION matched any `*.py` token in an orchestration text and surface._invoking_planes matched it by BASENAME, so a bare filename appearing in PROSE credited every file sharing that basename with the make and ci planes. The Makefile carries the sentence 'invisible to an __init__.py predicate' inside a comment, and that one comment made all 88 package initialisers in the repository report themselves invoked; model.py, config.py, registry.py, ledger.py and ten more inflated the count the same way. Requiring a script invocation to be a PATH (to contain a '/') and matching it as a full path corrected the measurement: the honest value is 53, not 33. A JUSTIFICATION WOULD HAVE BEEN THE WRONG INSTRUMENT -- it would have excused every future regression on this metric forever, when what changed was what the metric MEASURES. Re-seeding is recorded here so the drop is auditable instead of silent.

floors.reason: The two are engine/__init__.py (2 statements) and platform/__init__.py (15 statements, 4 imports). Both are ROOT package initialisers of trees measured per SUB-package, and that shape is what puts them outside every rule: coverage sources name engine.foundation and platform.identity, never engine or platform, so no source covers the initialiser itself. Naming the roots instead would admit engine.uicm — 1,893 statements with zero test files, declared exempt with a written reason — and convert a dead-code finding into a coverage figure, which is the measurement laundering the exemption register exists to prevent. Ω FOUND THESE: both were absent from coverage.xml under the enumerated denominator and no control could say so. WHAT CLOSES THIS FLOOR: retiring or testing engine.uicm, after which the roots can be measured whole and this metric reaches 0. That is an owner decision about dead code, not a coverage setting.

Artifacts whose top-level root is not a Python identifier — 00-MASTER, 00-BOOK and 00-CMG — so NO coverage source could name them, by the language's own rule for identifiers rather than by any policy here. They are governance engines: owned (Ω-2 derives an authority for every one), invoked (verify.sh stages, Makefile targets and workflows all reach them) and unmeasurable by coverage as currently laid out. WHAT CLOSES THIS FLOOR: making those engines importable under test rather than only executable as scripts, which is a real change to how they are structured and not a setting. Until then the population may fall and hold; it may never rise, because a floor accepts the stall and never a regression.

Artifacts no import, orchestration plane or entry point reaches. Declared as an OPEN FINDING rather than an acceptable state, so the number is argued about instead of tolerated. LOWERED 52 -> 51 BECAUSE THE FINDING WAS ACTED ON, NOT BECAUSE THE METRIC MOVED: the coverage programme admitted a suite that imports a module nothing had reached, so an artifact that read as dead is now reached by a test that runs. That is the second time this floor has fallen for exactly that reason, and the mechanism is the same both times - a floor is not a ceiling, and assert_floors_live refuses a declared floor the work has overtaken. TWENTY OF THE REMAINDER ARE __init__.py FILES, which is still the largest single group and the most tractable: a package initialiser that nothing imports is a package nothing imports. WHAT CLOSES THIS FLOOR: deleting what is finished and wiring what is not, which is a per-file owner decision. The bound still binds in the direction that matters - one more unreachable artifact REGRESSES and is refused, because a floor excuses the stall and never a regression.

how_to_read: best[m] is the lowest value of metric m this repository has ever recorded. A run measuring more than best[m] is REFUSED unless justifications names m with a reason. A justification permits one run and never moves best[m], so a regression cannot become the new normal by being explained. holds[m] counts consecutive runs at an unchanged value; a CONVERGENT metric held at a non-zero value for 5 runs is reported STALLED, because an exemption class that stops shrinking has become a convention. floors[m] argues that a particular value IS m's floor and so accepts the stall — it does NOT excuse a regression, and it is refused as stale the moment m is measured below it.
